chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who married a woman and did not specify a dower for her, then consummated the marriage with her: He said: 'For her is the dower of her womenfolk.'

key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: Consummation of marriage (entering into the marital bed)
key_terms.صَدَاقاً: Dower/Mahr (specifically in the indefinite form indicating an unspecified amount)
key_terms.صَدَاقُ نِسَائِهَا: The dower of her womenfolk (mahr al-mithl, i.e., standard dower for her peers)

ai.seo_question: What is the dower for a wife if no specific amount was agreed upon before consummation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that in the absence of an agreed-upon dower, consummation of the marriage triggers the entitlement to 'mahr al-mithl' (the dower of her equals). This ruling ensures the wife receives a fair, customary amount determined by her social status and family background, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on justice and preventing exploitation in marital contracts. The narration underscores the legal principle that marriage validity is not contingent upon the prior specification of mahr, but its payment becomes obligatory upon intimacy.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said regarding a man who married a woman and did not necessitate a dower for her, then copulated with her. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For her would be a dower of his womenfolk’.
en.sarwar: 10. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from more than one person from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah who has said the following:

“About the case of a man who marries a woman without assigning any mahr (dower) and goes to bed with her, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘She has a mahr (dower) similar to that for the women of her family.’”
